comparison: Both evaluate the baseline predictive model (C2, C11-C15). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical rigor, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the moderate C-index (0.60) adds value over simpler, cheaper biomarkers like NLR.

Both assess the combined baseline+on-treatment model (C3, C16-C22). OpenEval rates it SUPPORTED with improved C-index (0.69), while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the modest improvement justifies the labor-intensive, expensive assay compared to existing alternatives.

Both evaluate validation cohort results (C5, C25-C30). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to small sample size (n=9) and endpoint substitution (BOR vs PFS). Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating validation is 'not very convincing' with only 8 patients and no PFS data, requiring much broader validation.

Both address validation cohort composition (C61-C66). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for transparent documentation but notes high exclusion rate. Peer review incorporates these claims into their UNSUPPORTED evaluation of validation adequacy.

Both evaluate imaging mass cytometry findings (C31-C36, C67-C68). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED despite small sample size. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the correlations and colocalization data without specific concerns.

Both address cohort characteristics (C7-C10). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for clear documentation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about selection bias from large number of excluded patients and lack of comparison between studied and excluded patients.

Both evaluate mechanistic hypotheses (C56-C60). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting they are plausible but speculative without direct experimental evidence. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting them as reasonable interpretations without requiring additional validation.

Both assess statistical methodology (C69-C71). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for rigorous approach despite sample size limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, suggesting need for ML techniques to reduce complexity and more rigorous validation approaches.

Both evaluate core hypothesis (C54-C55). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on demonstrated improvement in predictive power. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED for clinical utility claims, questioning whether the labor-intensive assay adds value over existing biomarkers and noting lack of prospective validation.

Both assess main conclusions (C79-C80). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting proof-of-concept is established but clinical implementation requires additional validation. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, stating prospective validation is essential and overall impact seems limited.
